out.title: Sales: quotations, proposals, contracts, catalog and pricing
out.text:
Sales turns a deal into priced, approved documents: quotations (the price), Solution Proposals (the scope and story), and contracts, all priced from the product catalog.

**Quotations** (/sales/quotations)
- Statuses: draft, sent, accepted, signed, rejected, expired, superseded. Manual moves: draft → sent; sent → accepted, rejected or expired; accepted → rejected. "Approved" is never set by hand (the approval engine does it) and "signed" only comes from recording the customer's PO.
- A sent quotation past its valid-until date (plus sales.quotation.expire_grace_days) is marked expired by a daily job; its owner gets one "re-quote or close the deal?" reminder when it ended within sales.quotation.expired_nudge_days (older ones expire quietly).
- Only drafts can be edited (sales:create_quotation). Delete only draft, rejected or expired (sales:edit_quotation).
- **Approval**: the Owner approves a quotation unless every line is a catalog item at list price (a discount within the SKU's volume tier still counts as list). Every discounted line must say its discount type. Above the policy amount the Owner is also pinged on WhatsApp.
- **Send** (sales:send_quotation): passes the approval gate, then sends the QR-verified PDF by email or WhatsApp; the first send starts Nary's follow-up cadence.
- **Signed**: record the customer's PO (number, date or verbal) → signed; recurring lines create subscriptions.
- **Revise**: only a sent, expired or rejected quotation with no invoices or payment schedule; the original becomes superseded and a new draft revision (-N) is made.
- **Invoice from a quotation** (finance:create_invoice): only when sent, accepted or signed; commercial or proforma, in full or by milestone; never more than the quotation total.

**Solution Proposals** (/sales/proposals)
- Statuses: draft, review, approved, sent, superseded. Editable in draft or review.
- Flow: a fit check proposes discovery; discovery fills a requirements sheet on the deal; Nary drafts the proposal (no accuracy claims), its figures and an internal cost sheet; the Owner confirms, which proposes the quotation draft; the Owner approves every proposal; the proposal is sent together with its quotations.
- Cost sheet and rate card need sales:view_costs (changing the rate card: sales:manage_costs).

**Contracts** (/sales/contracts)
- Statuses: draft, sent_for_signing, signed, expired, terminated. Types: sales, service, msa, nda, partner_agreement, vendor_agreement.
- Moving to sent_for_signing or signed needs Owner approval (sales_contract policy); e-sign by the counterparty, 5 business days, extendable to 10. Completing the e-sign marks it signed.

**Catalog and pricing** (/sales/catalog)
- One SKU per sellable item; prices per currency with a valid-from date; volume tiers per SKU.
- A currency's own price row wins; otherwise it is converted from `catalog.conversion_base_currency` at the recorded FX rate, except currencies in `catalog.independent_currencies`, which never convert.
- **Tiers are private**: never applied automatically; a negotiation lever. A discount up to the tier still counts as list price.
- A manual price needs sales:price_manual and a deeper discount needs sales:apply_discount; either makes the quotation need Owner approval.
- Only a superadmin or the executive role edits the catalog; viewing needs sales:view_catalog.
- The chat sees the whole active catalog (SKU, how it is sold, list price) in its prompt; search_catalog gives one item's full detail.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
- **Quotation notes from the house template** (4 Nov 2026, Settings → Sales & CRM → Quotation notes templates): every quotation's notes are one numbered list of bold-labelled clauses in the house order, from the template of the lines' product family (the families of the templates in Settings; first match wins; an export currency adds the Incoterm of the template and swaps the Currency and Tax wording; English). To draft notes now: call quotation_notes_template (quotation_id, or items_json + currency) to see the family, the house clauses and the deal clauses with guidance, then pass ONLY the deal clauses to propose_quotation_draft / propose_quotation_update as notes_deal {clause_key: text} (scope, deliverables, client obligations, delivery, pilot credit 50 to 100% by context, payment_milestones for services). The ERP fills validity, currency, payment terms (and the quotation's payment_terms field: products 100% on order or 60/40 from sales.split_payment_min_unit_equivalents, services the down payment then milestones with the final payment on UAT and the handover certificate, invoices due in sales.quotation.notes.invoice_due_days days), hard stop, non-payment (projects and pilots), payment method, bank charges, tax (follows the line taxes), delivery (hardware: sales.quotation.notes.lead_days_min to _max working days), warranty (from delivery), Care from year 2 (sales.quotation.notes.care_pct) and acceptance. A house clause's wording changes only with notes_override (the Owner or sales:apply_discount); some take an added sentence, and optional ones are added with "include" (site_requirements; delay_penalties, the client-caused carve-out, only when a tender imposes penalties). Never an accuracy figure, never a delay penalty, a discount clause only when the Owner or the pricing permission asks. The check warns in the card and in the editor (Fill notes from template, the warnings panel), and the approval refuses a draft whose notes miss a required clause, are not numbered or break those rules (sales.quotation.notes.block_submit); sent or approved quotations are not re-checked. Free `notes` are still accepted, and checked.
- **Segments and pricing rules** (Settings → Sales & CRM → Pricing rules; CRM > segments): leads, deals and catalog items may carry an optional segment (the setting crm.segments lists the allowed values; empty means free text). A quotation line priced below sales.pricing_rules.min_cost_multiple x its catalog cost (custom and service lines against the labour of the deal's cost sheet) blocks the approval while sales.pricing_rules.block_submit is on, unless the Owner gives a pricing override with a reason (set_pricing_override); a missing cost only warns. A quotation with a proposed catalog price, or a SKU in sales.pricing_rules.owner_approval_skus, always goes to the Owner. Without sales:view_costs the check shows no figures.
- **Linking a quotation to a deal without a revision** (5 Nov 2026): a quotation made before its deal existed (sent, approved, accepted, signed, expired, or a draft) is linked to the deal with Link to deal on the quotation page (sales:create_quotation; POST /sales/quotations/{id}/link-deal) or with propose_quotation_link_deal (quotation, deal_id, set_deal_value default true; a card at Ask). Every revision of the quotation moves with it; by default the deal's value and currency become the total of its current revision, and the deal's timeline gets a "Quotation linked" activity with the value before and after (the deal it leaves gets one too). An accepted or signed quotation also gives the deal its offering line and Pilot flag, unless they were set by hand. The customer document never changes: no revision, no new approval, the same PDF, lines, terms and status. The deal must belong to the quotation's customer; a cancelled or superseded quotation is refused; the same deal again changes nothing. propose_quotation_update with only deal_id on a quotation that is no longer an editable draft answers with this card instead of refusing.

out.title: Where the settings live
out.text:
Every business number, rate, template and switch is a setting (Settings in the ERP), never fixed in code; a missing one stops the feature with a clear error naming the key. Values change, so read the live value through the feature, not from here. Keys by category:

## ai
- `ai.anthropic.api_key`: Anthropic API key (Claude); blank = ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
- `ai.assistant.catalog_digest_max_items`: AI chat: most products listed in its catalog overview (above this, families only)
- `ai.assistant.system_prompt`: Nary persona for the chat (how Nary thinks and advises)
- `ai.budget.essential_jobs`: AI budget: jobs that keep running past the stop threshold
- `ai.budget.hard_stop_pct`: AI budget: stop every job, essential ones too, at (%)
- `ai.budget.job_caps`: AI budget: optional monthly cap per job (USD)
- `ai.budget.monthly_usd`: AI budget: monthly cap in USD (0 = no cap)
- `ai.budget.stop_pct`: AI budget: stop non-essential jobs at (%)
- `ai.budget.warn_pct`: AI budget: warn the Owner at this share of the monthly cap (%)
- `ai.cache.default_ttl`: Prompt cache lifetime for jobs without their own (5m or 1h)
- `ai.erp_guide.enabled`: AI chat: keep the ERP guide (how the ERP works, built from the code) in AI Knowledge
- `ai.no_em_dash`: Remove em dashes from everything the AI writes
- `ai.pricing`: AI prices: model prefix → USD per 1M tokens (input, output, cache read, cache write)
- `ai.pricing.batch_discount_pct`: AI prices: Batch API discount (%)
- `ai.routing`: AI routing: job → provider, model, effort, max tokens
- `mcp.apply.require_totp`: MCP full power: nary_apply asks for the code from the authenticator app (customer messages, invoices, meetings, money, deletes and merges)
- `mcp.oauth.access_minutes`: MCP access: minutes an agent's login token lasts (it renews itself)
- `mcp.oauth.code_minutes`: MCP access: minutes a login code is valid during sign-in
- `mcp.oauth.refresh_days`: MCP access: days an agent stays logged in without being used
- `mcp.owner.confirm_minutes`: MCP full power: minutes a confirm code stays valid (the Owner's yes to a message, meeting or invoice)
- `mcp.pat.default_days`: MCP access: default lifetime of a personal token (days)

## branding
- `branding.favicon_data`: Favicon (base64 data URL, PNG/SVG/ICO)
- `branding.logo_image_data`: Logo Image (base64 data URL)

## crm
- `crm.activity.max_chars`: The longest note or activity text the CRM stores (characters); a longer one is refused, never cut
- `crm.activity_types`: CRM: activity types (JSON list of {key, label})
- `crm.deal_dup.window_days`: Two open deals of one contact or organization opened within this many days are checked as one deal
- `crm.dup.repropose_days`: Days after which a duplicate deal or lead pair whose merge card expired, failed or was withdrawn is proposed again
- `crm.email.relink_days`: Email threads of the last N days are linked to a contact made after the emails arrived

out.title: Approvals, QR verification, sending to clients and e-sign
out.text:
One approval engine decides every document that needs a yes; an approved document carries a QR code anyone can check, can be sent to the client from the ERP, and can be signed electronically.

**The engine** (/approvals, policies in Settings → Approvals & signing → Approval policies)
- Submit → route → approve or reject. The chain is fixed at submit; one pending request per document; rejecting needs a comment and makes the document editable again.
- An approval is bound to the document's facts: any edit after approval makes it stale and sending is refused until it is approved again.
- The send/activate gate: approved and unchanged → go; otherwise it submits (the Owner submitting approves at once) and answers "approval pending".
- Approver modes: the Owner (a superadmin whose position starts with Owner), a role (optionally in a department), the submitter's manager, a named user. The submitter can't approve their own request unless the step allows it (superadmins can).
- Default policies: quotation (Owner unless all at list price), proposal (Owner), invoice (Owner), contract (Owner, 48h SLA), purchase order (team lead up to the policy limit, Owner above; 2 vendor quotes above a second limit), contractor request (Owner), work order (Owner above the request's estimate), vendor invoice (Finance Admin up to 25M, Owner above), expense (manager, Finance Admin, Owner when large), marketing content, hiring request, offer letter, SOP article, payroll run (Owner).
- Hourly SLA reminders. Seeing requests needs approvals:view; editing policies needs approvals:manage_policies.

**Approval as signature and QR**
- A policy's signature flow: none, counterparty, internal, or internal then counterparty. With counterparty, the company's approval is its signature.
- Approved documents with QR enabled carry a QR on every page pointing to a public check page that re-validates on every scan (valid, revoked, superseded, expired, void, not approved). HR documents need a login. Issuing and revoking need verification:issue / verification:revoke.

**Sending to the client**: quotations, invoices, purchase orders, work orders and proposals are sent from the ERP by email or WhatsApp (each with its send permission), through the approval gate. The same document to the same person within 15 minutes needs confirming again.

**E-sign** (/sign/documents)
- A sign document is draft, pending, completed, declined, expired or cancelled; signers sign in order (pending, sent, viewed, signed, declined); completion produces a certificate.
- From an approved document, the ERP issues the verified PDF, places signature fields and invites the signers; the counterparty deadline is in business days and can be extended up to the policy's limit.
- When signing completes: a contract becomes signed; an offer letter becomes accepted (the applicant to offer_accepted); a quotation records its signing date (its status changes only by recording the PO).
- Permissions: sign:view, sign:send, sign:manage.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
- **Digital seal on every document sent** (3 Nov 2026): every approved document with a verification QR (quotations, invoices, purchase and work orders, proposals) leaves the ERP with the company's digital seal, a PAdES certification signature: the same sealed PDF goes by email and WhatsApp (also as Nary or MCP client attachments), and is what the public check page (/v/...) shows and downloads and what staff download. A PDF reader (Acrobat) shows it in its signature panel as certified by the company and flags any edit made after sealing; the text stays selectable and nothing is encrypted. The seal allows form filling and further signatures (DocMDP level 2), so a customer can still add their own digital signature. While the company uses its own self-signed certificate, Acrobat shows a yellow "validity unknown" banner (the seal is intact, its signer is not on Adobe's trust list); a certificate from a trusted certificate authority (Adobe-trusted) installed on the server is used automatically and removes it. The sealed copy is made at approval time; documents issued earlier are sealed on their next send or download while still valid. If sealing fails the unsealed copy goes out (its QR still verifies it) and the Owner gets one alert for that document. The check page says "Digitally sealed by" and the company name with the seal level. documents.seal.outbound (Settings → Approvals & signing → E-signing) turns it off. The e-sign flow still signs the unsealed original and seals the signed result as before.

out.title: HR: employees, attendance, leave, payroll, hiring and offers
out.text:
HR keeps the people side: employees and the org chart, attendance by face, leave, payroll with income tax and social contributions, and hiring from request to offer letter.

- **Employees** (/hr/employees, /hr/org-chart): active, probation, on_leave, terminated, resigned. hr:manage_employees edits, hr:view_all_employees sees everyone. Terminations: pending → confirmed → processed → completed (hr:initiate_termination).
- **Attendance** (/hr/attendance, kiosk page /clock): face clock-in from a personal phone (liveness challenge, key frames, GPS) or a registered kiosk (it matches locally, the server checks again). Records: present, absent, late, half_day, on_leave, holiday, remote. Overrides need hr:manage_attendance. Thresholds are settings (`hr.face_match_distance`, `hr.geo_max_accuracy_m`, `hr.work_start_time`).
- **Leave** (/hr/leave): pending → approved, rejected or cancelled; reviewing needs hr:approve_leave and nobody approves their own.
- **Payroll** (/hr/payroll): runs are draft → approved → paid (or cancelled). Creating a run (hr:manage_compensation) submits it for Owner approval; paying needs a still-valid approval and posts to the ledger. Income tax withholding, the year-end true-up, social contributions, allowances and brackets are settings (Settings → People & payroll).
- **Hiring** (/hr/hiring): a hiring request (hr:request_hire) goes to the Owner; approved → approved, rejected → on hold. Job openings (/hr/job-openings): draft, published, paused, closed, filled.
- **Applicants** (/hr/recruitment): applied, screening, phone_screen, interview_1, interview_2, technical_test, offer_sent, offer_accepted, offer_rejected, hired, rejected, withdrawn (hr:manage_applicants).
- **Offer letters** (/hr/offer-letters): draft → sent (needs Owner approval; the applicant becomes offer_sent) → accepted, declined or countered; can be cancelled from draft, sent or countered. E-signing completes it as accepted.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
- **Face check timeouts and attempts** (6 Nov 2026): the liveness check on a phone or the kiosk tablet gives each step its own time (find the face and hold still, do the action, face the camera again; `hr.face.step_timeouts_ms`, default 8 s, 10 s and 5 s), counted from when that step begins, and a phone's challenge stays valid `hr.face.challenge_ttl_seconds` (at least the steps' total plus 15 s for the upload). "Try again" reuses the open camera. Every check is counted (no photo or face data): HR > Attendance > Attempts shows the last 7 days by outcome (done, timeout, aborted), by device (kiosk or personal), by the step reached, and the timeout rate (GET /hr/attendance/face-attempts/summary?days=7, hr:view_attendance).
- **Passive face check first** (6 Nov 2026): when `hr.face.passive.enabled` is on, a phone or the kiosk tablet first flashes `hr.face.passive.flash_count` soft colours (`hr.face.passive.palette`, `hr.face.passive.flash_ms` each, never under 250 ms) and photographs the face after `hr.face.passive.settle_ms`; a live face reflects the colours (`hr.face.passive.flash_min_corr`, `hr.face.passive.flash_min_delta`) and an anti-spoof model scores the face as real (`hr.face.passive.spoof_min_real`). Phones are judged by the server (the colours are picked by the server), the kiosk judges itself and reports the result. When the check is not sure or fails, the blink or head turn follows in the same check. The clock event keeps the method (passive or active), the scores and the fallback reason; phone fallbacks count in Attempts as passive_inconclusive or passive_failed.

out.title: Overview: how Granary fits together
out.text:
Granary is an open-source ERP: CRM and sales, finance, projects, HR, manufacturing, procurement, partners, operations, knowledge and Nary (the AI assistant) in one system, with one approval engine and one permission model.

- **Money flow**: lead → deal → (proposal) → quotation → Owner approval when not at list price → sent to the customer → PO recorded (signed) → proforma or commercial invoice (Owner approves every invoice) → payment → general ledger. A Won deal is handed over to a project.
- **Approvals**: one engine for every document that needs a decision (quotations, invoices, contracts, POs, expenses, payroll, offer letters, SOPs...). Sending or activating a document goes through its gate; an edit after approval makes the approval stale. See approvals-and-signing.
- **Who may do what**: permission codes `module:action` grouped in roles (see permissions). Nary's tools act with the permissions of the person they act for.
- **Business numbers** (tax rates, social contributions, thresholds, reminders, prices rules) are settings, never fixed in code; a missing one stops the feature with a clear error naming the key (see settings).

out.title: CRM record fields a card may write
out.text:
What a change card (propose_record_change) may write on each CRM record, and what a create needs. Ids (`*_id`) must be real records (look them up) or `@ref` of a create card in the same answer.

## organization
Writable: address, city, country, description, email, employee_count, industry, name, notes, phone, postal_code, tax_id, website.
Required to create: name.

## contact
Writable: country, department, email, first_name, is_primary, last_name, linkedin_url, notes, organization_id, phone, position, whatsapp.
Required to create: first_name.

## lead
Writable: attribution, contact_id, currency, description, disqualification_reason, estimated_value, interested_products, organization_id, priority, source, source_campaign_id, source_detail, status, title.
Required to create: source.

## deal
Writable: actual_close_date, contact_id, currency, expected_close_date, loss_notes, loss_reason, loss_reasons, notes, organization_id, probability, product_line_ids, stage, title, value.
Required to create: title.

## activity
Writable: activity_type, contact_id, content, deal_id, direction, duration_minutes, entity_id, entity_type, lead_id, next_action, next_action_due, outcome, scheduled_at, subject.
Required to create: entity_type, entity_id, activity_type.

<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
## Also writable
- organization: quote_without_tax.
- lead: segment.
- deal: segment.
segment (leads and deals): optional, a value of the setting crm.segments when it lists any, otherwise free text. A new deal starts in its lead's segment.

out.title: Projects and R&D: delivery after a deal is won, and product development
out.text:
Projects deliver what was sold: a Won deal is handed over to a project with phases, milestones, tasks and time logs. R&D tracks the company's own product development.

- **Projects** (/projects): planning, active, on_hold, completed, cancelled. Creating needs projects:create (starts in planning); editing needs projects:edit; an active project can't be deleted. Status can be set freely (no fixed order). Seeing all projects needs projects:view_all, otherwise only your own.
- **Phases** (not_started, in_progress, completed, skipped) and **milestones** (pending, achieved, missed, waived; projects:manage_milestones).
- **Tasks** (/projects/tasks): todo, in_progress, review, done, cancelled, with a priority.
- **Time logs** (/projects/time-logs): logging needs projects:log_time, seeing everyone's needs projects:view_time; cost uses `projects.monthly_hours` and `projects.default_hourly_cost`.
- **Handoff from a Won deal**: Nary writes a handoff package on the deal and proposes a kickoff card. Applying it creates one installation project in planning, with the PM and Tech Lead from Nary's role table, the deal value as budget and the kickoff tasks from `nary.handoff.kickoff_tasks`.
- **R&D** (/rnd/projects, /rnd/backlog, /rnd/product-lines): R&D projects (active, paused, archived), sprints, a backlog (backlog → refined → in_sprint → in_progress → review → done, or rejected/deferred), releases and GitLab pipelines. Permissions rnd:view and rnd:manage.

out.title: Nary: the AI sales and operations assistant
out.text:
Nary is the ERP's AI assistant: it answers staff in the chat (web and WhatsApp), runs the sales playbooks with customers, and proposes actions the Owner approves.

- **Cards and autonomy** (page Nary → Autonomy, /nary/autonomy): everything Nary does to the world is an action with a level: 0 Shadow (a draft only, nobody told), 1 Ask (a card the Owner approves at /nary/approvals or by number on WhatsApp), 2 Act and tell (done, then the Owner is told), 3 Silent (done, not told). The levels are stored in the settings nary.autonomy.levels; nary.autonomy.never_promote lists the actions that are never promoted past Ask (money and customer messages by default; the Owner can change the list). Approving without edits builds a streak that can promote an action; rejecting demotes it. On WhatsApp the Owner confirms a money decision (nary.owner.confirm_twice_actions) a second time on its final version. What the Owner asks for in the chat follows the same page: a customer message is a card at Ask and goes out right after the answer at Act and tell (whatsapp.reply.send, email.reply.send); cancelling a meeting, adding guests and merging contacts (meeting.cancel, meeting.add_guests, contact.merge) are a card at Ask, done at once at Act and tell, and only a draft at Shadow. nary_owner_context shows every action's current level: read it rather than guess.
- **Quiet hours on WhatsApp** (the working hours in nary.working_hours): outside them Nary sends customers only the acknowledgement of a new conversation. Its other WhatsApp messages (a reply at Act and tell, a meeting reminder, a booking's confirmation) are not lost: the card becomes "scheduled" (Approvals → Scheduled for the morning) and goes out at the start of the next working period; the Owner is told when, and "1" sends it now, Drop drops it. Whatever the Owner approves or asks for (a card applied by number, on Approvals or over MCP, or "send it" in the chat) goes out at once, at any hour; only an approved draft still waits while someone has the chat on the phone (it was written before they took over). Email has no quiet hours.
- **Shadow mode** (Nary → Overview): while on, every customer message Nary writes stays a draft (the acknowledgement and meeting booking are exempt). Pause stops Nary completely ("Nary pause" on WhatsApp).
- **Channels**: WhatsApp (privacy gate: chats saved on the phone but unknown to the CRM wait for the Owner's "business or personal"; personal chats are never read), the CRM inbox hello@ (new mail is triaged; a new prospect becomes a lead; a returning contact waits for the Owner), and web forms (Web3forms).
- **Playbooks**: triage, acknowledgement, BANT scoring, the reply play (price answers at list price only, quotation consults with the Owner, meetings, objections), follow-up cadence after a quotation, contract and handoff at Won, partner watch.
- **The Owner on WhatsApp**: Nary raises one topic at a time (approvals, consults, questions, hot leads, failures, briefs); the Owner answers in words or by number; "next" brings the next topic, "cukup" stops a long answer.
- **Sending as Nary**: when the Owner says "send it", Nary shows the final text and sends it after the confirmation, signed with the WhatsApp signature from Settings (email: the company signature filled as Nary), in the customer's thread. A chat Nary can't write into (a staff or personal chat, one the customer never wrote in, the hourly or daily limit) is said when the card is prepared, not after the yes. A send that still fails raises an alert to the Owner with the reason from the WhatsApp service or the mail server, and the card shows that reason.
- **Numbers on WhatsApp**: a number answers the cards that were on the person's phone when they sent it: the latest list of cards (a later message from Nary without cards doesn't take them away; cards older than nary.staff_chat.card_window_minutes do lapse). A numbered notice (an approval's 1 apply / 2 view / 3 skip) answers numbers only until Nary writes anything newer; after that a number goes to Nary, which reads it against what it said last. So "1" on WhatsApp confirms a card: there is no need to open the ERP. Numbers that don't fit that list ("1 2 3 4" against one card) apply nothing and the list is shown again. A "Done" or "Not done" line under a card comes from the system, not from Nary: before explaining one, Nary checks the chat (get_whatsapp_messages) and reports what actually happened. Messages are answered one at a time, in order; a message the live feed missed is answered when the gap check finds it, marked late (a late bare number is not applied), and the Owner is told the feed is dropping messages.
- **Cards Nary can take back**: withdraw_cards takes back Nary's own waiting cards; a new message card to the same person replaces the older one. Other small cards: link a WhatsApp chat to a contact (propose_chat_link; a chat also links itself once the contact's phone or WhatsApp number is saved), and move, finish or cancel a follow-up reminder (propose_reminder_change). Calls and notes are logged as an activity (propose_record_change, object_type activity); a lead's summary goes in its description.
- **Meetings at an agreed time**: "add the meeting with Diana tomorrow 11:00 to our calendar and send her the link" is one card (propose_meeting): on confirm a Google Calendar event on the company calendar with a Google Meet link, Google's invitations to the company people named and the customer's email, a meeting activity on the deal or lead, and the customer's WhatsApp or email as Nary with {link} replaced by the Meet link. The Owner and sales staff can book; only someone with nary:approve can have Nary send the message (otherwise they send the link themselves). These meetings get the Owner's brief 30 minutes before and the debrief prompt, but no automatic reminders to the customer. When no time is agreed yet, Nary's own slot offer (three times, the customer picks) is used instead. Bookings show in Nary → Meetings. If the message can't go out, the meeting stays booked and the result says why and hands back the Meet link; the invitation can be sent again later without a new event (list_meetings, then propose_customer_message with meeting_id).
- **Attachments**: an email Nary sends can carry approved sales documents (a quotation, an invoice, a solution proposal with its quotations) as their verified PDFs; an unapproved one goes for approval first and the email waits. Other files can't be attached yet.
- **Reply alerts**: when a customer answers one of our messages (Nary's, the Owner's or one typed on the phone) on WhatsApp or by email to hello@, Nary notes who answered and what they said. When it needs something from us, the Owner hears of it on WhatsApp within minutes (working hours), with Nary's reply card when the playbook made one (1 sends it); replies that need nothing go in the next morning or wrap-up brief. Settings nary.reply_alerts.enabled and nary.reply_alerts.mode (action_needed or every_reply).
- **Meetings already booked**: list_meetings shows them with their Meet links. A guest who sends their email later is added to the Google event (propose_meeting_guests: Google sends the real invitation); a meeting is cancelled with propose_meeting_cancel (Google tells the invitees, the meeting and its activity are marked cancelled, no more briefs, optional message to the customer). A meeting deleted in Google Calendar is noticed before its reminder or brief and marked cancelled.
- **Duplicate contacts**: propose_contact_merge merges two contacts that are one person (the same engine as CRM → Duplicates: everything moves to the one kept, empty fields are filled, the duplicate goes).
- **Follow-ups**: reminders that fall due together arrive as one WhatsApp per person (Settings → Sales & CRM → Follow-up reminders → Follow-ups per WhatsApp); a lead counts as active while there are WhatsApp messages or emails on it.
- **WhatsApp history import** (Nary → History): the Owner ticks personal chats first; the rest are imported slowly (a few chats per run, newest first). A chat the import hasn't reached yet is taken in on the spot when Nary is asked to message it (its newest messages, silently; the rest comes first in line), and **Import now** on a chat's row does the same. Nary still writes only into chats where the customer has written (whoever wrote first), never into personal or staff chats; when it can't, it says the exact reason.
- **Memory**: customer notes, company facts and the style guide learnt from the Owner's own WhatsApp replies and sent emails, in two sections (On WhatsApp, By email), re-learnt monthly and approved by the Owner in Nary → Memory.
- **Learning**: Nary writes procedures it worked out as skills (propose_skill); the Owner approves them in Nary → Memory → Skills; approved skills are listed in its prompt and read with use_skill. When no tool can do something, it files the idea in the R&D backlog (propose_tool_idea, project in `nary.skills.tool_ideas_project`); it never writes code.
- **Catalog**: Nary sees the whole active catalog; tiers, white-label rules, cost and margin only when the person it helps may see costs (sales:view_costs).
- **Pages**: /nary (Overview), /nary/chat, /nary/approvals, /nary/intake, /nary/memory. Permissions nary:view, nary:approve, nary:manage.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Oct 2026) -->
- **Solution Proposal from the chat**: propose_solution_proposal (a deal, a promoted lead or an organization's one open deal, plus what is known: standard and custom items, options A/B, assumptions, notes) is one card; on confirm Nary writes the requirements sheet, drafts the proposal, makes its figures and the internal cost sheet, and answers with the preview link (cost only for sales:view_costs). update_requirements changes the sheet of an existing proposal.
- **Quotations**: list_quotations (by customer, deal, status, currency, dates, owner; paged) and get_quotation (lines, totals, notes, approval and send history; margin only for sales:view_costs).
- **Duplicate organizations**: find_duplicate_organizations groups organizations whose names match once legal forms (Ltd, Inc, LLC), case and punctuation are ignored, with what tells them apart; propose_organization_merge (one kept, one or more merged) moves everything that points at them (contacts, leads, deals, activities, quotations, invoices, projects, emails, research, documents) and fills empty fields; the card lists what moves.
- **Card history**: list_nary_cards shows Nary's cards by status (applied, edited, rejected, expired, cancelled, pending), with the drafted and the final text, who decided and the Owner's reason for a rejection. Read it before repeating a draft the Owner rejected.
- **Deleting a contact**: propose_contact_delete, for the Owner only; a contact with open deals or quotations is refused unless they are listed on the card.
- **Messages at a set time**: propose_customer_message with send_at ("2026-10-21 13:30", company time, at most nary.send_at.max_days ahead) sends at that time, re-checked and re-greeted at the moment it goes out; cancel_scheduled_message lists or cancels them.
- **After a meeting**: the results go to the deal (not the old promoted lead) as a "Meeting results" note, follow-ups land on the deal, and a stage or value change from the transcript comes as a card. get_activity_history reads the timeline of a lead, deal, contact or organization (activities, emails, WhatsApp by day, meetings, quotations, stage changes, follow-ups). Gemini meeting notes in Google Docs can't be read yet.
- **Staff mailboxes**: search_emails with mailbox ('me', a staff member's name or email, or 'all') searches the personal mailboxes connected in the email client, inbox and sent; get_mailbox_email reads one email with its conversation. Everyone may read their own mailbox; another person's needs email:read_staff_mailboxes (the Owner). Every such read is in the audit log, and with nary.mailboxes.notify_o
…(cut; ask for a narrower topic)

topics.title: API map
topics.summary: Every API route by area, so you know what the ERP can do.

topics.title: Approvals, QR verification, sending to clients and e-sign
topics.summary: One approval engine decides every document that needs a yes; an approved document carries a QR code anyone can check, can be sent to the client from the ERP, and can be signed electronically.

topics.title: CRM: organisations, contacts, leads, deals, activities, inboxes
topics.summary: The CRM holds who the company sells to and where each opportunity stands: organisations and their contacts, leads (unqualified interest) and deals (qualified opportunities moving through stages), with activities, follow-ups and the shared i

topics.title: CRM picklists (allowed values)
topics.summary: The exact keys for deal stages, lead statuses and moves, sources, priorities, reasons and activity types.

topics.title: CRM record fields a card may write
topics.summary: The writable fields of organizations, contacts, leads, deals and activities, and what a create needs.

topics.title: Finance: invoices, payments, schedules, expenses, ledger, tax, FX, assets, budgets
topics.summary: Finance bills customers, records what is paid, reimburses expenses and keeps the general ledger, with taxes and exchange rates from settings.

topics.title: HR: employees, attendance, leave, payroll, hiring and offers
topics.summary: HR keeps the people side: employees and the org chart, attendance by face, leave, payroll with income tax and social contributions, and hiring from request to offer letter.

topics.title: Knowledge base, SOPs and AI Knowledge
topics.summary: Two libraries: the Knowledge Base for people (articles and SOPs, which also ground the AI), and AI Knowledge, documents only the AI reads (price rules, playbooks, product facts, and this ERP guide).

topics.title: Manufacturing and inventory: BOMs, production, units, QC, warranty, stock
topics.summary: Manufacturing builds the company's hardware: bills of materials, production orders, a registry of every unit with its QC, warranty and RMA, and the stock it uses.

topics.title: Marketing: campaigns, content calendar, email marketing
topics.summary: Marketing plans campaigns, publishes content through approval, and sends email campaigns with a global unsubscribe.

topics.title: Nary: the AI sales and operations assistant
topics.summary: Nary is the ERP's AI assistant: it answers staff in the chat (web and WhatsApp), runs the sales playbooks with customers, and proposes actions the Owner approves.

topics.title: Operations: helpdesk, maintenance, fleet
topics.summary: The operations modules keep customers supported and the company's own equipment and vehicles running.

topics.title: Overview: how Granary fits together
topics.summary: Granary is an open-source ERP: CRM and sales, finance, projects, HR, manufacturing, procurement, partners, operations, knowledge and Nary (the AI assistant) in one system, with one approval engine and one permission model.

topics.title: Procurement (vendors, RFQs, POs, receipts, vendor invoices) and partners
topics.summary: Procurement buys what the company needs from vendors and contractors; partner management runs the resellers who sell the company's products (deal registrations, commissions, MDF).

topics.title: Projects and R&D: delivery after a deal is won, and product development
topics.summary: Projects deliver what was sold: a Won deal is handed over to a project with phases, milestones, tasks and time logs. R&D tracks the company's own product development.

topics.title: Roles and permission codes
topics.summary: Which roles exist and every permission code (module:action) with what it allows.

topics.title: Sales: quotations, proposals, contracts, catalog and pricing
topics.summary: Sales turns a deal into priced, approved documents: quotations (the price), Solution Proposals (the scope and story), and contracts, all priced from the product catalog.

topics.title: Settings, users and roles

section_synced.topic: how do invoices and payments work

out.title: Finance: invoices, payments, schedules, expenses, ledger, tax, FX, assets, budgets
out.text:
Finance bills customers, records what is paid, reimburses expenses and keeps the general ledger, with taxes and exchange rates from settings.

**Invoices** (/finance/invoices)
- Types: commercial, proforma, credit_note, debit_note. Statuses: draft, sent, partially_paid, paid, overdue, cancelled, refunded (also superseded and converted for proformas).
- **Issuing** (draft → sent, finance:send_invoice): the Owner approves every invoice and credit note first (WhatsApp ping above the policy amount); the approver is stamped as authorised by. A commercial invoice is then posted to the ledger.
- Manual moves: sent, partially_paid or overdue → paid (finance:mark_paid); draft → cancelled; an unpaid sent/overdue proforma → cancelled.
- Overdue is set daily for sent or partially paid invoices past due, with reminder emails on the `finance.invoice_reminder_days` schedule.
- A sent proforma can be revised (superseded + new draft). A commercial invoice is never revised: issue a credit note (full reversal, one per invoice; anything already paid becomes refund due). A proforma converts to a commercial invoice.
- Creating needs finance:create_invoice.

**Payments** (/finance/payments): recorded as confirmed (finance:confirm_payment) against a sent invoice (not a draft, cancelled, superseded, converted or a credit note); the invoice becomes paid or partially paid and the payment is posted. A payment can be reversed.

**Payment schedules** (/finance/schedules): milestones of a quotation (on order, delivery, milestone or date; pending, invoiced, paid, overdue, waived). Raising a proforma for a milestone marks it invoiced.

**Expenses** (/finance/expenses): submitted as pending (finance:submit_expense); approval chain line manager → Finance Admin → Owner when the claim or one of its lines is over the policy limits or the FX rate is missing; claims over the pre-approval limit must be pre-approved. Approved expenses post to the ledger; reimbursing needs finance:confirm_payment. A new claim goes to its approval chain the moment it is saved (tick "pre-approved" above the pre-approval limit, or it is refused); the Approve/Reject buttons act on that chain.

**Ledger** (/finance/journal, /finance/periods, /finance/accounts, /finance/reports)
- Journal entries: draft, posted, reversed. Post, unpost and reverse need finance:post_journal; lines balance per currency; the period must be open (a locked period blocks posting).
- Automatic posting (invoice issued, payment, credit note, refund, vendor bill, expense, payroll, depreciation, disposal) only from `finance.gl_autopost_from` (blank = off), using the account role mappings; an unmapped role is an error.

**Tax, FX, bank, assets, budget**
- Taxes are records (for example VAT10, a withholding tax on services, payroll income tax); default sales tax per currency in `finance.default_sales_tax`. Managed at /finance/taxes (finance:manage_tax_config).
- Exchange rates sync every 6 hours (the active currencies, for example USD, EUR, GBP, JPY) and can be entered by hand (finance:manage_fx); a quotation keeps the rate of its issue date.
- Bank reconciliation (/finance/bank, finance:manage_bank): reconcile only when every line is matched or excluded.
- Fixed assets (finance:manage_assets): depreciation and disposal post to the ledger.
- Budgets (finance:manage_budget): draft → approved → active → closed; lines editable only in draft.

out.title: Sales: quotations, proposals, contracts, catalog and pricing
out.text:
Sales turns a deal into priced, approved documents: quotations (the price), Solution Proposals (the scope and story), and contracts, all priced from the product catalog.

**Quotations** (/sales/quotations)
- Statuses: draft, sent, accepted, signed, rejected, expired, superseded. Manual moves: draft → sent; sent → accepted, rejected or expired; accepted → rejected. "Approved" is never set by hand (the approval engine does it) and "signed" only comes from recording the customer's PO.
- A sent quotation past its valid-until date (plus sales.quotation.expire_grace_days) is marked expired by a daily job; its owner gets one "re-quote or close the deal?" reminder when it ended within sales.quotation.expired_nudge_days (older ones expire quietly).
- Only drafts can be edited (sales:create_quotation). Delete only draft, rejected or expired (sales:edit_quotation).
- **Approval**: the Owner approves a quotation unless every line is a catalog item at list price (a discount within the SKU's volume tier still counts as list). Every discounted line must say its discount type. Above the policy amount the Owner is also pinged on WhatsApp.
- **Send** (sales:send_quotation): passes the approval gate, then sends the QR-verified PDF by email or WhatsApp; the first send starts Nary's follow-up cadence.
- **Signed**: record the customer's PO (number, date or verbal) → signed; recurring lines create subscriptions.
- **Revise**: only a sent, expired or rejected quotation with no invoices or payment schedule; the original becomes superseded and a new draft revision (-N) is made.
- **Invoice from a quotation** (finance:create_invoice): only when sent, accepted or signed; commercial or proforma, in full or by milestone; never more than the quotation total.

**Solution Proposals** (/sales/proposals)
- Statuses: draft, review, approved, sent, superseded. Editable in draft or review.
- Flow: a fit check proposes discovery; discovery fills a requirements sheet on the deal; Nary drafts the proposal (no accuracy claims), its figures and an internal cost sheet; the Owner confirms, which proposes the quotation draft; the Owner approves every proposal; the proposal is sent together with its quotations.
- Cost sheet and rate card need sales:view_costs (changing the rate card: sales:manage_costs).

**Contracts** (/sales/contracts)
- Statuses: draft, sent_for_signing, signed, expired, terminated. Types: sales, service, msa, nda, partner_agreement, vendor_agreement.
- Moving to sent_for_signing or signed needs Owner approval (sales_contract policy); e-sign by the counterparty, 5 business days, extendable to 10. Completing the e-sign marks it signed.

**Catalog and pricing** (/sales/catalog)
- One SKU per sellable item; prices per currency with a valid-from date; volume tiers per SKU.
- A currency's own price row wins; otherwise it is converted from `catalog.conversion_base_currency` at the recorded FX rate, except currencies in `catalog.independent_currencies`, which never convert.
- **Tiers are private**: never applied automatically; a negotiation lever. A discount up to the tier still counts as list price.
- A manual price needs sales:price_manual and a deeper discount needs sales:apply_discount; either makes the quotation need Owner approval.
- Only a superadmin or the executive role edits the catalog; viewing needs sales:view_catalog.
- The chat sees the whole active catalog (SKU, how it is sold, list price) in its prompt; search_catalog gives one item's full detail.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
- **Quotation notes from the house template** (4 Nov 2026, Settings → Sales & CRM → Quotation notes templates): every quotation's notes are one numbered list of bold-labelled clauses in the house order, from the template of the lines' product family (the families of the templates in Settings; first match wins; an export currency adds the Incoterm of the template and swaps the Currency and Tax wording; English). To draft notes now: call quotation_notes_template (quotation_id, or items_json + currency) to see the family, the house clauses and the deal clauses with guidance, then pass ONLY the deal clauses to propose_quotation_draft / propose_quotation_update as notes_deal {clause_key: text} (scope, deliverables, client obligations, delivery, pilot credit 50 to 100% by context, payment_milestones for services). The ERP fills validity, currency, payment terms (and the quotation's payment_terms field: products 100% on order or 60/40 from sales.split_payment_min_unit_equivalents, services the down payment then milestones with the final payment on UAT and the handover certificate, invoices due in sales.quotation.notes.invoice_due_days days), hard stop, non-payment (projects and pilots), payment method, bank charges, tax (follows the line taxes), delivery (hardware: sales.quotation.notes.lead_days_min to _max working days), warranty (from delivery), Care from year 2 (sales.quotation.notes.care_pct) and acceptance. A house clause's wording changes only with notes_override (the Owner or sales:apply_discount); some take an added sentence, and optional ones are added with "include" (site_requirements; delay_penalties, the client-caused carve-out, only when a tender imposes penalties). Never an accuracy figure, never a delay penalty, a discount clause only when the Owner or the pricing permission asks. The check warns in the card and in the editor (Fill notes from template, the warnings panel), and the approval refuses a draft whose notes miss a required clause, are not numbered or break those rules (sales.quotation.notes.block_submit); sent or approved quotations are not re-checked. Free `notes` are still accepted, and checked.
- **Segments and pricing rules** (Settings → Sales & CRM → Pricing rules; CRM > segments): leads, deals and catalog items may carry an optional segment (the setting crm.segments lists the allowed values; empty means free text). A quotation line priced below sales.pricing_rules.min_cost_multiple x its catalog cost (custom and service lines against the labour of the deal's cost sheet) blocks the approval while sales.pricing_rules.block_submit is on, unless the Owner gives a pricing override with a reason (set_pricing_override); a missing cost only warns. A quotation with a proposed catalog price, or a SKU in sales.pricing_rules.owner_approval_skus, always goes to the Owner. Without sales:view_costs the check shows no figures.
- **Linking a quotation to a deal without a revision** (5 Nov 2026): a quotation made before its deal existed (sent, approved, accepted, signed, expired, or a draft) is linked to the deal with Link to deal on the quotation page (sales:create_quotation; POST /sales/quotations/{id}/link-deal) or with propose_quotation_link_deal (quotation, deal_id, set_deal_value default true; a card at Ask). Every revision of the quotation moves with it; by default the deal's value and currency become the total of its current revision, and the deal's timeline gets a "Quotation linked" activity with the value before and after (the deal it leaves gets one too). An accepted or signed quotation also gives the deal its offering line and Pilot flag, unless they were set by hand. The customer document never changes: no revision, no new approval, the same PDF, lines, terms and status. The deal must belong to the quotation's customer; a cancelled or superseded quotation is refused; the same deal again changes nothing. propose_quotation_update with only deal_id on a quotation that is no longer an editable draft answers with this card instead of refusing.

out.title: Where the settings live
out.text:
Every business number, rate, template and switch is a setting (Settings in the ERP), never fixed in code; a missing one stops the feature with a clear error naming the key. Values change, so read the live value through the feature, not from here. Keys by category:

## ai
- `ai.anthropic.api_key`: Anthropic API key (Claude); blank = ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
- `ai.assistant.catalog_digest_max_items`: AI chat: most products listed in its catalog overview (above this, families only)
- `ai.assistant.system_prompt`: Nary persona for the chat (how Nary thinks and advises)
- `ai.budget.essential_jobs`: AI budget: jobs that keep running past the stop threshold
- `ai.budget.hard_stop_pct`: AI budget: stop every job, essential ones too, at (%)
- `ai.budget.job_caps`: AI budget: optional monthly cap per job (USD)
- `ai.budget.monthly_usd`: AI budget: monthly cap in USD (0 = no cap)
- `ai.budget.stop_pct`: AI budget: stop non-essential jobs at (%)
- `ai.budget.warn_pct`: AI budget: warn the Owner at this share of the monthly cap (%)
- `ai.cache.default_ttl`: Prompt cache lifetime for jobs without their own (5m or 1h)
- `ai.erp_guide.enabled`: AI chat: keep the ERP guide (how the ERP works, built from the code) in AI Knowledge
- `ai.no_em_dash`: Remove em dashes from everything the AI writes
- `ai.pricing`: AI prices: model prefix → USD per 1M tokens (input, output, cache read, cache write)
- `ai.pricing.batch_discount_pct`: AI prices: Batch API discount (%)
- `ai.routing`: AI routing: job → provider, model, effort, max tokens
- `mcp.apply.require_totp`: MCP full power: nary_apply asks for the code from the authenticator app (customer messages, invoices, meetings, money, deletes and merges)
- `mcp.oauth.access_minutes`: MCP access: minutes an agent's login token lasts (it renews itself)
- `mcp.oauth.code_minutes`: MCP access: minutes a login code is valid during sign-in
- `mcp.oauth.refresh_days`: MCP access: days an agent stays logged in without being used
- `mcp.owner.confirm_minutes`: MCP full power: minutes a confirm code stays valid (the Owner's yes to a message, meeting or invoice)
- `mcp.pat.default_days`: MCP access: default lifetime of a personal token (days)

- `crm.deal_dup.window_days`: Two open deals of one contact or organization opened within this many days are checked as one deal

out.title: Approvals, QR verification, sending to clients and e-sign
out.text:
One approval engine decides every document that needs a yes; an approved document carries a QR code anyone can check, can be sent to the client from the ERP, and can be signed electronically.

**The engine** (/approvals, policies in Settings → Approvals & signing → Approval policies)
- Submit → route → approve or reject. The chain is fixed at submit; one pending request per document; rejecting needs a comment and makes the document editable again.
- An approval is bound to the document's facts: any edit after approval makes it stale and sending is refused until it is approved again.
- The send/activate gate: approved and unchanged → go; otherwise it submits (the Owner submitting approves at once) and answers "approval pending".
- Approver modes: the Owner (a superadmin whose position starts with Owner), a role (optionally in a department), the submitter's manager, a named user. The submitter can't approve their own request unless the step allows it (superadmins can).
- Default policies: quotation (Owner unless all at list price), proposal (Owner), invoice (Owner), contract (Owner, 48h SLA), purchase order (team lead up to the policy limit, Owner above; 2 vendor quotes above a second limit), contractor request (Owner), work order (Owner above the request's estimate), vendor invoice (Finance Admin up to 25M, Owner above), expense (manager, Finance Admin, Owner when large), marketing content, hiring request, offer letter, SOP article, payroll run (Owner).
- Hourly SLA reminders. Seeing requests needs approvals:view; editing policies needs approvals:manage_policies.

**Approval as signature and QR**
- A policy's signature flow: none, counterparty, internal, or internal then counterparty. With counterparty, the company's approval is its signature.
- Approved documents with QR enabled carry a QR on every page pointing to a public check page that re-validates on every scan (valid, revoked, superseded, expired, void, not approved). HR documents need a login. Issuing and revoking need verification:issue / verification:revoke.

**Sending to the client**: quotations, invoices, purchase orders, work orders and proposals are sent from the ERP by email or WhatsApp (each with its send permission), through the approval gate. The same document to the same person within 15 minutes needs confirming again.

**E-sign** (/sign/documents)
- A sign document is draft, pending, completed, declined, expired or cancelled; signers sign in order (pending, sent, viewed, signed, declined); completion produces a certificate.
- From an approved document, the ERP issues the verified PDF, places signature fields and invites the signers; the counterparty deadline is in business days and can be extended up to the policy's limit.
- When signing completes: a contract becomes signed; an offer letter becomes accepted (the applicant to offer_accepted); a quotation records its signing date (its status changes only by recording the PO).
- Permissions: sign:view, sign:send, sign:manage.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
- **Digital seal on every document sent** (3 Nov 2026): every approved document with a verification QR (quotations, invoices, purchase and work orders, proposals) leaves the ERP with the company's digital seal, a PAdES certification signature: the same sealed PDF goes by email and WhatsApp (also as Nary or MCP client attachments), and is what the public check page (/v/...) shows and downloads and what staff download. A PDF reader (Acrobat) shows it in its signature panel as certified by the company and flags any edit made after sealing; the text stays selectable and nothing is encrypted. The seal allows form filling and further signatures (DocMDP level 2), so a customer can still add their own digital signature. While the company uses its own self-signed certificate, Acrobat shows a yellow "validity unknown" banner (the seal is intact, its signer is not on Adobe's trust list); a certificate from a trusted certificate authority (Adobe-trusted) installed on the server is used automatically and removes it. The sealed copy is made at approval time; documents issued earlier are sealed on their next send or download while still valid. If sealing fails the unsealed copy goes out (its QR still verifies it) and the Owner gets one alert for that document. The check page says "Digitally sealed by" and the company name with the seal level. documents.seal.outbound (Settings → Approvals & signing → E-signing) turns it off. The e-sign flow still signs the unsealed original and seals the signed result as before.

out.title: HR: employees, attendance, leave, payroll, hiring and offers
out.text:
HR keeps the people side: employees and the org chart, attendance by face, leave, payroll with income tax and social contributions, and hiring from request to offer letter.

- **Employees** (/hr/employees, /hr/org-chart): active, probation, on_leave, terminated, resigned. hr:manage_employees edits, hr:view_all_employees sees everyone. Terminations: pending → confirmed → processed → completed (hr:initiate_termination).
- **Attendance** (/hr/attendance, kiosk page /clock): face clock-in from a personal phone (liveness challenge, key frames, GPS) or a registered kiosk (it matches locally, the server checks again). Records: present, absent, late, half_day, on_leave, holiday, remote. Overrides need hr:manage_attendance. Thresholds are settings (`hr.face_match_distance`, `hr.geo_max_accuracy_m`, `hr.work_start_time`).
- **Leave** (/hr/leave): pending → approved, rejected or cancelled; reviewing needs hr:approve_leave and nobody approves their own.
- **Payroll** (/hr/payroll): runs are draft → approved → paid (or cancelled). Creating a run (hr:manage_compensation) submits it for Owner approval; paying needs a still-valid approval and posts to the ledger. Income tax withholding, the year-end true-up, social contributions, allowances and brackets are settings (Settings → People & payroll).
- **Hiring** (/hr/hiring): a hiring request (hr:request_hire) goes to the Owner; approved → approved, rejected → on hold. Job openings (/hr/job-openings): draft, published, paused, closed, filled.
- **Applicants** (/hr/recruitment): applied, screening, phone_screen, interview_1, interview_2, technical_test, offer_sent, offer_accepted, offer_rejected, hired, rejected, withdrawn (hr:manage_applicants).
- **Offer letters** (/hr/offer-letters): draft → sent (needs Owner approval; the applicant becomes offer_sent) → accepted, declined or countered; can be cancelled from draft, sent or countered. E-signing completes it as accepted.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Nov 2026) -->
- **Face check timeouts and attempts** (6 Nov 2026): the liveness check on a phone or the kiosk tablet gives each step its own time (find the face and hold still, do the action, face the camera again; `hr.face.step_timeouts_ms`, default 8 s, 10 s and 5 s), counted from when that step begins, and a phone's challenge stays valid `hr.face.challenge_ttl_seconds` (at least the steps' total plus 15 s for the upload). "Try again" reuses the open camera. Every check is counted (no photo or face data): HR > Attendance > Attempts shows the last 7 days by outcome (done, timeout, aborted), by device (kiosk or personal), by the step reached, and the timeout rate (GET /hr/attendance/face-attempts/summary?days=7, hr:view_attendance).
- **Passive face check first** (6 Nov 2026): when `hr.face.passive.enabled` is on, a phone or the kiosk tablet first flashes `hr.face.passive.flash_count` soft colours (`hr.face.passive.palette`, `hr.face.passive.flash_ms` each, never under 250 ms) and photographs the face after `hr.face.passive.settle_ms`; a live face reflects the colours (`hr.face.passive.flash_min_corr`, `hr.face.passive.flash_min_delta`) and an anti-spoof model scores the face as real (`hr.face.passive.spoof_min_real`). Phones are judged by the server (the colours are picked by the server), the kiosk judges itself and reports the result. When the check is not sure or fails, the blink or head turn follows in the same check. The clock event keeps the method (passive or active), the scores and the fallback reason; phone fallbacks count in Attempts as passive_inconclusive or passive_failed.

out.title: Overview: how Granary fits together
out.text:
Granary is an open-source ERP: CRM and sales, finance, projects, HR, manufacturing, procurement, partners, operations, knowledge and Nary (the AI assistant) in one system, with one approval engine and one permission model.

- **Money flow**: lead → deal → (proposal) → quotation → Owner approval when not at list price → sent to the customer → PO recorded (signed) → proforma or commercial invoice (Owner approves every invoice) → payment → general ledger. A Won deal is handed over to a project.
- **Approvals**: one engine for every document that needs a decision (quotations, invoices, contracts, POs, expenses, payroll, offer letters, SOPs...). Sending or activating a document goes through its gate; an edit after approval makes the approval stale. See approvals-and-signing.
- **Who may do what**: permission codes `module:action` grouped in roles (see permissions). Nary's tools act with the permissions of the person they act for.
- **Business numbers** (tax rates, social contributions, thresholds, reminders, prices rules) are settings, never fixed in code; a missing one stops the feature with a clear error naming the key (see settings).
- **Sections of this guide**: crm, sales, finance, approvals-and-signing, projects, hr, manufacturing, partners-and-vendors, operations, marketing, knowledge-and-ai, nary, settings-and-roles; generated: crm-picklists, crm-fields, permissions, settings, api.

out.title: CRM record fields a card may write
out.text:
What a change card (propose_record_change) may write on each CRM record, and what a create needs. Ids (`*_id`) must be real records (look them up) or `@ref` of a create card in the same answer.

## organization
Writable: address, city, country, description, email, employee_count, industry, name, notes, phone, postal_code, tax_id, website.
Required to create: name.

## contact
Writable: country, department, email, first_name, is_primary, last_name, linkedin_url, notes, organization_id, phone, position, whatsapp.
Required to create: first_name.

## lead
Writable: attribution, contact_id, currency, description, disqualification_reason, estimated_value, interested_products, organization_id, priority, source, source_campaign_id, source_detail, status, title.
Required to create: source.

## deal
Writable: actual_close_date, contact_id, currency, expected_close_date, loss_notes, loss_reason, loss_reasons, notes, organization_id, probability, product_line_ids, stage, title, value.
Required to create: title.

## activity
Writable: activity_type, contact_id, content, deal_id, direction, duration_minutes, entity_id, entity_type, lead_id, next_action, next_action_due, outcome, scheduled_at, subject.
Required to create: entity_type, entity_id, activity_type.

out.title: Projects and R&D: delivery after a deal is won, and product development
out.text:
Projects deliver what was sold: a Won deal is handed over to a project with phases, milestones, tasks and time logs. R&D tracks the company's own product development.

- **Projects** (/projects): planning, active, on_hold, completed, cancelled. Creating needs projects:create (starts in planning); editing needs projects:edit; an active project can't be deleted. Status can be set freely (no fixed order). Seeing all projects needs projects:view_all, otherwise only your own.
- **Phases** (not_started, in_progress, completed, skipped) and **milestones** (pending, achieved, missed, waived; projects:manage_milestones).
- **Tasks** (/projects/tasks): todo, in_progress, review, done, cancelled, with a priority.
- **Time logs** (/projects/time-logs): logging needs projects:log_time, seeing everyone's needs projects:view_time; cost uses `projects.monthly_hours` and `projects.default_hourly_cost`.
- **Handoff from a Won deal**: Nary writes a handoff package on the deal and proposes a kickoff card. Applying it creates one installation project in planning, with the PM and Tech Lead from Nary's role table, the deal value as budget and the kickoff tasks from `nary.handoff.kickoff_tasks`.
- **R&D** (/rnd/projects, /rnd/backlog, /rnd/product-lines): R&D projects (active, paused, archived), sprints, a backlog (backlog → refined → in_sprint → in_progress → review → done, or rejected/deferred), releases and GitLab pipelines. Permissions rnd:view and rnd:manage.

out.title: Nary: the AI sales and operations assistant
out.text:
Nary is the ERP's AI assistant: it answers staff in the chat (web and WhatsApp), runs the sales playbooks with customers, and proposes actions the Owner approves.

- **Cards and autonomy** (page Nary → Autonomy, /nary/autonomy): everything Nary does to the world is an action with a level: 0 Shadow (a draft only, nobody told), 1 Ask (a card the Owner approves at /nary/approvals or by number on WhatsApp), 2 Act and tell (done, then the Owner is told), 3 Silent (done, not told). The levels are stored in the settings nary.autonomy.levels; nary.autonomy.never_promote lists the actions that are never promoted past Ask (money and customer messages by default; the Owner can change the list). Approving without edits builds a streak that can promote an action; rejecting demotes it. On WhatsApp the Owner confirms a money decision (nary.owner.confirm_twice_actions) a second time on its final version. What the Owner asks for in the chat follows the same page: a customer message is a card at Ask and goes out right after the answer at Act and tell (whatsapp.reply.send, email.reply.send); cancelling a meeting, adding guests and merging contacts (meeting.cancel, meeting.add_guests, contact.merge) are a card at Ask, done at once at Act and tell, and only a draft at Shadow. nary_owner_context shows every action's current level: read it rather than guess.
- **Quiet hours on WhatsApp** (the working hours in nary.working_hours): outside them Nary sends customers only the acknowledgement of a new conversation. Its other WhatsApp messages (a reply at Act and tell, a meeting reminder, a booking's confirmation) are not lost: the card becomes "scheduled" (Approvals → Scheduled for the morning) and goes out at the start of the next working period; the Owner is told when, and "1" sends it now, Drop drops it. Whatever the Owner approves or asks for (a card applied by number, on Approvals or over MCP, or "send it" in the chat) goes out at once, at any hour; only an approved draft still waits while someone has the chat on the phone (it was written before they took over). Email has no quiet hours.
- **Shadow mode** (Nary → Overview): while on, every customer message Nary writes stays a draft (the acknowledgement and meeting booking are exempt). Pause stops Nary completely ("Nary pause" on WhatsApp).
- **Channels**: WhatsApp (privacy gate: chats saved on the phone but unknown to the CRM wait for the Owner's "business or personal"; personal chats are never read), the CRM inbox hello@ (new mail is triaged; a new prospect becomes a lead; a returning contact waits for the Owner), and web forms (Web3forms).
- **Playbooks**: triage, acknowledgement, BANT scoring, the reply play (price answers at list price only, quotation consults with the Owner, meetings, objections), follow-up cadence after a quotation, contract and handoff at Won, partner watch.
- **The Owner on WhatsApp**: Nary raises one topic at a time (approvals, consults, questions, hot leads, failures, briefs); the Owner answers in words or by number; "next" brings the next topic, "cukup" stops a long answer.
- **Sending as Nary**: when the Owner says "send it", Nary shows the final text and sends it after the confirmation, signed with the WhatsApp signature from Settings (email: the company signature filled as Nary), in the customer's thread. A chat Nary can't write into (a staff or personal chat, one the customer never wrote in, the hourly or daily limit) is said when the card is prepared, not after the yes. A send that still fails raises an alert to the Owner with the reason from the WhatsApp service or the mail server, and the card shows that reason.
- **Numbers on WhatsApp**: a number answers the cards that were on the person's phone when they sent it: the latest list of cards (a later message from Nary without cards doesn't take them away; cards older than nary.staff_chat.card_window_minutes do lapse). A numbered notice (an approval's 1 apply / 2 view / 3 skip) answers numbers only until Nary writes anything newer; after that a number goes to Nary, which reads it against what it said last. So "1" on WhatsApp confirms a card: there is no need to open the ERP. Numbers that don't fit that list ("1 2 3 4" against one card) apply nothing and the list is shown again. A "Done" or "Not done" line under a card comes from the system, not from Nary: before explaining one, Nary checks the chat (get_whatsapp_messages) and reports what actually happened. Messages are answered one at a time, in order; a message the live feed missed is answered when the gap check finds it, marked late (a late bare number is not applied), and the Owner is told the feed is dropping messages.
- **Cards Nary can take back**: withdraw_cards takes back Nary's own waiting cards; a new message card to the same person replaces the older one. Other small cards: link a WhatsApp chat to a contact (propose_chat_link; a chat also links itself once the contact's phone or WhatsApp number is saved), and move, finish or cancel a follow-up reminder (propose_reminder_change). Calls and notes are logged as an activity (propose_record_change, object_type activity); a lead's summary goes in its description.
- **Meetings at an agreed time**: "add the meeting with Diana tomorrow 11:00 to our calendar and send her the link" is one card (propose_meeting): on confirm a Google Calendar event on the company calendar with a Google Meet link, Google's invitations to the company people named and the customer's email, a meeting activity on the deal or lead, and the customer's WhatsApp or email as Nary with {link} replaced by the Meet link. The Owner and sales staff can book; only someone with nary:approve can have Nary send the message (otherwise they send the link themselves). These meetings get the Owner's brief 30 minutes before and the debrief prompt, but no automatic reminders to the customer. When no time is agreed yet, Nary's own slot offer (three times, the customer picks) is used instead. Bookings show in Nary → Meetings. If the message can't go out, the meeting stays booked and the result says why and hands back the Meet link; the invitation can be sent again later without a new event (list_meetings, then propose_customer_message with meeting_id).
- **Attachments**: an email Nary sends can carry approved sales documents (a quotation, an invoice, a solution proposal with its quotations) as their verified PDFs; an unapproved one goes for approval first and the email waits. Other files can't be attached yet.
- **Reply alerts**: when a customer answers one of our messages (Nary's, the Owner's or one typed on the phone) on WhatsApp or by email to hello@, Nary notes who answered and what they said. When it needs something from us, the Owner hears of it on WhatsApp within minutes (working hours), with Nary's reply card when the playbook made one (1 sends it); replies that need nothing go in the next morning or wrap-up brief. Settings nary.reply_alerts.enabled and nary.reply_alerts.mode (action_needed or every_reply).
- **Meetings already booked**: list_meetings shows them with their Meet links. A guest who sends their email later is added to the Google event (propose_meeting_guests: Google sends the real invitation); a meeting is cancelled with propose_meeting_cancel (Google tells the invitees, the meeting and its activity are marked cancelled, no more briefs, optional message to the customer). A meeting deleted in Google Calendar is noticed before its reminder or brief and marked cancelled.
- **Duplicate contacts**: propose_contact_merge merges two contacts that are one person (the same engine as CRM → Duplicates: everything moves to the one kept, empty fields are filled, the duplicate goes).
- **Follow-ups**: reminders that fall due together arrive as one WhatsApp per person (Settings → Sales & CRM → Follow-up reminders → Follow-ups per WhatsApp); a lead counts as active while there are WhatsApp messages or emails on it.
- **WhatsApp history import** (Nary → History): the Owner ticks personal chats first; the rest are imported slowly (a few chats per run, newest first). A chat the import hasn't reached yet is taken in on the spot when Nary is asked to message it (its newest messages, silently; the rest comes first in line), and **Import now** on a chat's row does the same. Nary still writes only into chats where the customer has written (whoever wrote first), never into personal or staff chats; when it can't, it says the exact reason.
- **Memory**: customer notes, company facts and the style guide learnt from the Owner's own WhatsApp replies and sent emails, in two sections (On WhatsApp, By email), re-learnt monthly and approved by the Owner in Nary → Memory.
- **Learning**: Nary writes procedures it worked out as skills (propose_skill); the Owner approves them in Nary → Memory → Skills; approved skills are listed in its prompt and read with use_skill. When no tool can do something, it files the idea in the R&D backlog (propose_tool_idea, project in `nary.skills.tool_ideas_project`); it never writes code.
- **Catalog**: Nary sees the whole active catalog; tiers, white-label rules, cost and margin only when the person it helps may see costs (sales:view_costs).
- **Pages**: /nary (Overview), /nary/chat, /nary/approvals, /nary/intake, /nary/memory. Permissions nary:view, nary:approve, nary:manage.
<!-- added after the Python freeze (Oct 2026) -->
- **Solution Proposal from the chat**: propose_solution_proposal (a deal, a promoted lead or an organization's one open deal, plus what is known: standard and custom items, options A/B, assumptions, notes) is one card; on confirm Nary writes the requirements sheet, drafts the proposal, makes its figures and the internal cost sheet, and answers with the preview link (cost only for sales:view_costs). update_requirements changes the sheet of an existing proposal.
- **Quotations**: list_quotations (by customer, deal, status, currency, dates, owner; paged) and get_quotation (lines, totals, notes, approval and send history; margin only for sales:view_costs).
- **Duplicate organizations**: find_duplicate_organizations groups organizations whose names match once legal forms (Ltd, Inc, LLC), case and punctuation are ignored, with what tells them apart; propose_organization_merge (one kept, one or more merged) moves everything that points at them (contacts, leads, deals, activities, quotations, invoices, projects, emails, research, documents) and fills empty fields; the card lists what moves.
- **Card history**: list_nary_cards shows Nary's cards by status (applied, edited, rejected, expired, cancelled, pending), with the drafted and the final text, who decided and the Owner's reason for a rejection. Read it before repeating a draft the Owner rejected.
- **Deleting a contact**: propose_contact_delete, for the Owner only; a contact with open deals or quotations is refused unless they are listed on the card.
- **Messages at a set time**: propose_customer_message with send_at ("2026-10-21 13:30", company time, at most nary.send_at.max_days ahead) sends at that time, re-checked and re-greeted at the moment it goes out; cancel_scheduled_message lists or cancels them.
- **After a meeting**: the results go to the deal (not the old promoted lead) as a "Meeting results" note, follow-ups land on the deal, and a stage or value change from the transcript comes as a card. get_activity_history reads the timeline of a lead, deal, contact or organization (activities, emails, WhatsApp by day, meetings, quotations, stage changes, follow-ups). Gemini meeting notes in Google Docs can't be read yet.
- **Staff mailboxes**: search_emails with mailbox ('me', a staff member's name or email, or 'all') searches the personal mailboxes connected in the email client, inbox and sent; get_mailbox_email reads one email with its conversation. Everyone may read their own mailbox; another person's needs email:read_staff_mailboxes (the Owner). Every such read is in the audit log, and with nary.mailboxes.notify_o
